title: Projective Hom graph parameter and generic point closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian integral scheme with function field $K$ and generic point $\eta$. Let $W\to S$ be H-projective, flat and finitely presented, and let $Q\to S$ be H-projective. Choose a closed immersion $W\times_SQ\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$. The functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_T(W\times_ST,Q\times_ST)$ is represented by a scheme $M=\coprod_P M_P$, where $P$ ranges over numerical Hilbert polynomials for the chosen embedding. There are H-projective finite-type $S$-schemes $H_P$ and open immersions $M_P\hookrightarrow H_P$, and a universal evaluation $W\times_SM\to Q\times_SM$ whose representing bijections commute with arbitrary base change. For every $K$-morphism $u:W_\eta\to Q_\eta$, its corresponding point $m:\operatorname{Spec}K\to M$ lies in one $M_P$. Its reduced closure $R\subset M$ is a closed subscheme of that $M_P$, integral, separated and of finite type and locally of finite presentation over $S$. There is a canonical identification $R_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ compatible with $m$, and $k(R)=K$. Restricting universal evaluation to $R$ extends $u$ on this generic fibre. No nodal-fibre, normality or no-rational-maps assumption is made.

Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Schemes, integrality, function fields, H-projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, properness and separatedness, finite type, fibre products, and closed and open immersions use [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-sc-function-field], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. Reduced closure means the topological closure endowed with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The morphism functor is [def-sfb-relative-morphisms-presheaf]. A numerical Hilbert polynomial is the polynomial eventually equal to the dimension of the degree-$n$ homogeneous coordinate space of a geometric fibre. Quasi-projective here means open in an H-projective $S$-scheme.

proof.text: Put $E=W\times_SQ$ with the embedding given in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability]: $S$ is Noetherian and $E$ is a closed subscheme of the specified projective space, so its Hilbert functor is represented by $H=\coprod_PH_P$, with $H_P$ H-projective, separated and finite type over $S$. Its universal closed family and classifying bijections commute with arbitrary base change. This theorem explicitly requires no flatness of $E$; none is inferred from $Q$.

source.place: 0D1A, graph ambient; projective Hilbert input as stated in the cited representability node

proof.text: By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $W\to S$ is proper and $Q\to S$ is proper, hence separated by the definition of properness. The other two graph-open hypotheses on $W$ are exactly its assumed flatness and finite presentation. Thus [lem-sfb-graphs-open-in-hilbert] applies to $Z=W,X=Q$. On the represented Hilbert functor of Step 1 it gives an open subscheme $M\subset H$ representing $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_T(W_T,Q_T)$, its universal evaluation, and the natural classifying bijections under arbitrary base change. The proper-Hilbert and projective-Hilbert functors here agree: each closed subscheme of $E_T$ is proper over $T$ because $E_T$ is proper. Indeed $E\to S$ is H-projective by the chosen embedding, hence proper; apply proper base change and the closed-subscheme clause of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Both functors impose precisely flatness and finite presentation in addition.

Set $M_P=M\cap H_P$. Each $H_P$ is both open and closed in the coproduct $H$, so $M=\coprod_PM_P$ and $M_P\hookrightarrow H_P$ is open. The image $x$ of the single point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ under the classifying map $m$ belongs to exactly one component $M_P$; the morphism factors through this open because its whole image lies there. As $M_P$ is also closed in $M$, the topological closure $C=\overline{\{x\}}$ in $M$ is contained in $M_P$ and agrees with its closure there.

source.place: 0D1B; elementary component decomposition and factorization through an open

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] on the closed subset $C$ to construct $R\hookrightarrow M$. Its restriction to the open-and-closed $M_P$ is the same reduced induced closed subscheme, by the affine radical-ideal formula and uniqueness in that node. Thus $R\hookrightarrow M_P$ is closed. The closure of one point is nonempty and irreducible: if it is contained in a union of two closed subsets, $x$ belongs to one of them, and then its entire closure does. Since $R$ is reduced, the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] proves that $R$ is integral, with generic point $x$.

Each $H_P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $H_P\to S$ is finite type and $S$ is Noetherian. Its underlying space has the minimal condition on closed subsets by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], hence the descending-chain condition: the range of any strictly descending chain would have no minimal member. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset is quasi-compact. In particular every inverse image of an affine open of $H_P$ under $M_P\hookrightarrow H_P$ is quasi-compact. This open immersion is therefore quasi-compact and is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The closed immersion $R\to M_P$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply finite-type composition twice to obtain that $R\to S$ is finite type. Finally $S$ is locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $R\to S$ locally of finite presentation.

source.place: 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); topology.tex 04ZA; locally finite presentation over a locally Noetherian base

proof.text: The inclusion $i:R\to H_P$ is a monomorphism: it is the composite of a closed immersion with an open immersion, each identifying the source with a subscheme. Consequently $R\times_{H_P}R=R$. The pullback of the closed diagonal $H_P\to H_P\times_SH_P$ along $i\times_Si$ is therefore exactly $\Delta_{R/S}:R\to R\times_SR$. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. This proves separatedness over $S$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here the closedness of the diagonal of $H_P/S$ is supplied by Step 1; no separatedness of $S$ over a ground field is assumed.

source.place: 01JP (fibre-product universal property), 01KK (separated diagonal); morphisms.tex 01QR (base change of closed immersions)

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $M_P$ over $V$ containing $x$. Such affines cover $R$: every nonempty open of $R=\overline{\{x\}}$ contains $x$, and every affine open of the integral $S$ contains $\eta$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] on $S$, identify $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The point $m$ gives an $A$-algebra map $\phi:B\to K$. Its kernel $\mathfrak p$ is prime, and the closure of $x$ in $U$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$: the point is the prime $\mathfrak p$, whose specializations are precisely primes containing it. The affine radical-ideal description in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] therefore gives $R\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak p)$. The map $m$ factors through this chart via the injection $B/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow K$. These factorizations agree on overlaps because their composites into $M$ are $m$ and closed immersions are monomorphisms; they define $m_R:\operatorname{Spec}K\to R$.

source.place: 01J3 affine formula for the reduced closure of a point; morphisms.tex 01RV, function field on an integral affine open

proof.text: Write $D=B/\mathfrak p\subset K$ on each chart from Step 7. This subring contains the image of $A$, and that image is injective because the composite $A\to D\to K$ is the canonical inclusion. Inverting $A\setminus\{0\}$ in $D$ gives exactly $K$: it is a subring of $K$ and contains every fraction $a/b$ from $\operatorname{Frac}A=K$. More explicitly, $D\otimes_AK\to K$ sends $d\otimes(a/b)$ to $da/b$, and its inverse sends $a/b$ to $1\otimes(a/b)$; the first composite is the identity, while the second is the identity because every $d\in D\subset K$ is a fraction from $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] these are precisely the affine charts of $R_\eta$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies them with the inverse images of $R\cap U$. Every such chart contains the image of $m_R$, and overlaps use the same map into $K$, so their identifications glue to $R_\eta\simeq\operatorname{Spec}K$, with $m_R$ on the generic fibre the inverse isomorphism. Also $\operatorname{Frac}D=K$, since $A\subset D\subset K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to the nonempty affine open $R\cap U$ of the integral $R$ to identify $k(R)=K$ canonically over $K$.

Pull back the evaluation of Step 2 along $R\hookrightarrow M$. By the classifying bijection, its pullback along $m_R$ is $u$, because the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\xrightarrow{m_R}R\to M$ is the original point $m$. Step 8 identifies this pullback with the generic fibre $R_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. The restricted evaluation therefore extends precisely $u$. The construction used neither nodal fibres nor normality nor a prohibition on rational maps.
